name: setup-bedrock
description: 'Wire @warlock.js/ai-bedrock — new BedrockSDK({region, apiKey?, credentials?, provider?}) for AWS Bedrock Converse API + Titan embeddings. AWS credential chain or an Amazon Bedrock API key (bearer). .model({name, vision?, reasoning?, promptCaching?, pdf?, audio?}) with cost-truth capabilities inferred per family, extended thinking via options.reasoning → Converse thinking budget_tokens, prompt caching via options.cacheControl → cachePoint on tools (Claude), system and the last message, 1h TTL via promptCacheTtl, usage inputIncludesCache: false + cachedTokens/cacheWriteTokens/cacheWrite1hTokens, built-in Claude prices for global./us. profiles (BEDROCK_GLOBAL_PRICING, BEDROCK_US_PRICING, bedrockPricingFor), ServiceUnavailableException → ProviderOverloadedError. # `@warlock.js/ai-bedrock`

Provider adapter that turns AWS Bedrock's **Converse API** into a vendor-neutral `ModelContract`, plus an Amazon **Titan** embedder. One wire mapping covers every Bedrock family.

## Construction

```ts
import { BedrockSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-bedrock";

// Ambient AWS credential chain (env vars / SSO / IAM role):
const bedrock = new BedrockSDK({ region: "us-east-1" });

// Explicit static credentials:
const bedrock2 = new BedrockSDK({
  region: "us-east-1",
  credentials: { accessKeyId: "AKIA...", secretAccessKey: "..." },
  provider: "bedrock-eu",
});

// Amazon Bedrock API key (bearer auth, no AWS credentials):
const bedrock3 = new BedrockSDK({
  apiKey: process.env.BEDROCK_API_KEY!,
  region: "us-east-1",
});
```

Bedrock authenticates via the **AWS credential chain** or an **Amazon Bedrock API key**. `apiKey` sends `Authorization: Bearer <key>` instead of a SigV4 signature (the adapter sets the AWS SDK's `token` + `authSchemePreference: ["httpBearerAuth"]`); combining it with `credentials` or `token`, or passing an empty key, throws `InvalidRequestError`. Without `apiKey`, the AWS SDK still reads a key from `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` on its own. `region` is required; `credentials` is optional (omit to use the standard provider chain). The whole config object is forwarded to `BedrockRuntimeClient`, so any AWS client option (`endpoint`, `requestHandler`, retry config) is accepted. `provider` defaults to `"bedrock"`.

## Producing a model

`name` is the Bedrock **model id or inference-profile id**:

```ts
bedrock.model({ name: "anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0" });
bedrock.model({ name: "us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0", temperature: 0.2 });
bedrock.model({ name: "meta.llama3-1-8b-instruct-v1:0", maxTokens: 1024 });
```

Uses the model-agnostic **Converse / ConverseStream** API — one wire mapping covers every Bedrock family (Claude, Nova, Llama, Mistral, Cohere) instead of per-family `InvokeModel` body shapes.

## Capabilities — what's auto-set

| Flag               | Default                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `structuredOutput` | `true` (via Converse `outputConfig.textFormat`)                                                                                                        |
| `vision`           | Inferred from model id substring. `true` for Claude 3/3.5/3.7/4, Nova Lite/Pro/Premier, Llama 3.2-11B/90B, Llama 4.                                    |
| `reasoning`        | Inferred from model id. `true` for Claude 3.7 + Claude 4 (Sonnet/Opus/Haiku) — they expose a configurable thinking budget on Converse.                 |
| `promptCaching`    | Inferred from model id. `true` for Claude 3.5+/3.7/4/5 and Nova 2 Lite / Micro / Lite / Pro / Premier — the families that honor Converse `cachePoint`. |
| `pdf`              | Inferred from model id. `true` for Claude 3+ and Nova Lite/Pro/Premier (Converse `document` blocks).                                                   |
| `audio`            | `false` by default — Converse does not accept audio blocks for the families this adapter targets. Pass `audio: true` for a confirmed audio model.      |

Explicit config always wins — every flag is overridable per model, e.g. `bedrock.model({ name, reasoning: false, promptCaching: true, pdf: false, audio: true })`.

## Reasoning / extended thinking

For a `reasoning`-capable model (Claude 3.7 / 4), `ModelCallOptions.reasoning` maps to Converse's escape hatch `additionalModelRequestFields.thinking = { type: "enabled", budget_tokens }`:

```ts
// Explicit thinking budget (token cap):
await model.complete(messages, { reasoning: { maxTokens: 2048 } });

// Effort tier → conventional budget (low 1024 / medium 4096 / high 16384):
await model.complete(messages, { reasoning: { effort: "high" } });
```

`maxTokens` wins over `effort` when both are set. For non-reasoning models — or when neither `effort` nor `maxTokens` is given — the option is a no-op, so unsupported params never reach the wire. Bedrock's Converse `TokenUsage` reports no reasoning-token channel, so `usage.reasoningTokens` is left unset (reasoning text arrives as `reasoningContent` content blocks, not a token count).

A thinking budget below `1024` throws before the request. When thinking is enabled and no output cap is configured, Converse receives `maxTokens = thinking budget + 4096`; an explicit `maxTokens` must be greater than the budget. On tool calls, Converse `reasoningContent` is retained and replayed automatically on the next turn through provider metadata. The stored shape is JSON-safe: signed reasoning text stays text, while redacted reasoning bytes are base64 encoded, so persisted history preserves the opaque block exactly.

## Prompt caching

For a `promptCaching`-capable model, `ModelCallOptions.cacheControl.breakpoints` (any positive value) places a Converse `cachePoint` on every stable segment of the prefix, in the order Bedrock processes them (`tools` → `system` → `messages`, three of the four checkpoints it allows):

| Segment  | Where the `cachePoint` goes             | Models                                               |
| -------- | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| tools    | after the last `toolConfig.tools` entry | Claude only — Nova accepts no cache point in `tools` |
| system   | after the system blocks                 | every caching-capable model                          |
| messages | appended to the LAST message            | every caching-capable model                          |

The lifetime is the per-call `cacheControl.ttl`, else the model's `promptCacheTtl`. `ttl: "1h"` is sent only to models that accept it — Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet / Opus 4.5+ and every Claude 5 family; any other model gets the 5-minute default, because AWS warns that the field "can result in a ValidationException" on 5-minute-only models.

```ts
import { BedrockSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-bedrock";

const bedrock = new BedrockSDK({ region: "us-east-1" });
const model = bedrock.model({ name: "global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6", promptCacheTtl: "1h" });

// tools + system + last message are cached for an hour:
await model.complete(
  [
    { role: "system", content: "Long, stable instructions…" },
    { role: "user", content: "First question" },
  ],
  { cacheControl: { breakpoints: 1 } },
);

// Per call, the TTL can be overridden:
await model.complete([{ role: "user", content: "hi" }], {
  cacheControl: { breakpoints: 1, ttl: "5m" },
});
```

Source for the placement rules and TTL support: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html (checked 2026-10-17). No-ops gracefully when the model is not caching-capable or no breakpoint was requested. Read-side accounting works without any breakpoint — see the usage section below.

## System prompt

Converse has no `"system"` role in `messages`. The adapter hoists every neutral `role: "system"` message into the separate `system: SystemContentBlock[]` request field. Transparent to the agent.

## Tool calls

- Outgoing: neutral tools → `toolConfig.tools[].toolSpec` with a JSON `inputSchema`. No tools → `toolConfig` omitted entirely (Bedrock rejects an empty `tools` array).
- Assistant tool calls in history → `assistant` message with optional leading `{ text }` + one `{ toolUse }` block per call.
- Tool results (`role: "tool"`) → a `user` turn with one `{ toolResult: { toolUseId, content: [{ text }] } }` block.
- Response `toolUse` blocks → neutral `toolCalls`; `stopReason: "tool_use"` → `finishReason: "tool_calls"`.

## Structured output

Object-root `responseSchema` + `structuredOutput`-capable → `outputConfig.textFormat = { type: "json_schema", structure: { jsonSchema: { name, schema } } }` — note Bedrock wants the schema as a **stringified JSON document**.

## Multipart messages (vision)

- `{ type: "text" }` → `{ text }`
- `{ type: "image", source: { base64, mediaType } }` → `{ image: { format, source: { bytes } } }` (base64 decoded; media type → `jpeg`/`png`/`gif`/`webp`)
- `{ type: "image", source: { url } }` → **throws `InvalidRequestError`**. Bedrock's `ImageSource` only accepts raw bytes or an S3 location. Resolve images to base64 first.

## Streaming

`model.stream()` drains `ConverseStreamCommand`'s `response.stream`:

- `contentBlockDelta.delta.text` → `{ type: "delta", content }`
- `toolUse`: `contentBlockStart` opens an accumulator, `contentBlockDelta.delta.toolUse.input` fragments append, `contentBlockStop` emits one consolidated `{ type: "tool-call", ... }`
- terminal `{ type: "done", finishReason, usage }` — usage from `metadata.usage` (a `TokenUsage`), including `cachedTokens` / `cacheWriteTokens` when reported (see the usage table below)
- opt-in (`options.streamChunks`, set by `agent.stream()`): `{ type: "reasoning", delta }` per `reasoningContent.text` delta, `{ type: "tool-args", callId, name, delta }` per client `toolUse.input` delta; no `usage` chunk (usage arrives once at the end)

**System tools:** `ai.providerTool({ provider: "bedrock", definition: { systemTool: { name: "nova_grounding" } } })` is appended to `toolConfig.tools` verbatim. `toolUse` blocks with `type: "server_tool_use"` are never dispatched as tool calls.

```ts
const grounding = ai.providerTool({
  provider: "bedrock",
  definition: { systemTool: { name: "nova_grounding" } },
});
ai.agent({ model: bedrock.model({ name: "us.amazon.nova-premier-v1:0" }), tools: [grounding] });
```

## Finish-reason mapping

`end_turn` / `stop_sequence` → `stop` · `max_tokens` → `length` · `tool_use` → `tool_calls` · `content_filtered` / `guardrail_intervened` / unknown / null → `error`.

## Embeddings — Amazon Titan only

```ts
const embedder = bedrock.embedder({ name: "amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0" });
const { vector } = await embedder.embed("Hello world");
const { vectors } = await embedder.embedMany(["a", "b"]); // N sequential calls
```

Targets the **Titan Text Embeddings** family via `InvokeModel`. **Titan has no batch endpoint** — `embedMany` issues one request per input sequentially and aggregates token usage. Cohere-on-Bedrock batch embeddings use an incompatible body shape and are out of scope — use the OpenAI adapter when batch throughput matters.

Pass `dimensions` to forward Titan v2's truncation hint (256 / 512 / 1024).

## Errors

Raw AWS SDK exceptions are wrapped into the typed `@warlock.js/ai` `AIError` hierarchy. Dispatch keys on the Smithy exception `name`:

- `AccessDeniedException` / 401 / 403 → `ProviderAuthError`
- `ThrottlingException` / 429 → `ProviderRateLimitError`
- `ServiceQuotaExceededException` → `QuotaExceededError`
- `ValidationException` with "too long / context window" → `ContextLengthExceededError`, else `InvalidRequestError`
- `ModelTimeoutException` / `ETIMEDOUT` → `ProviderTimeoutError`
- `ServiceUnavailableException` / 503 → `ProviderOverloadedError` (`code: "PROVIDER_OVERLOADED"`, `retryable: true`) — the service is temporarily unable to serve the request
- other 5xx / `ModelError` → `ProviderError`

Every wrapped error carries `status`, `retryable` and `billed` (`false` for 401 / 402 / 403, otherwise `"unknown"` — AWS publishes no rule for failed requests). `fallbackModel` fails over on `PROVIDER_OVERLOADED` by default.

## Token counting

```ts
await bedrock.count("some text"); // approximate heuristic, offline
```

Per-model tokenizers differ across Bedrock families.

## Pricing — built-in Claude prices and registry

All rates are **USD per 1,000,000 tokens** (`ModelPricing`: `input`, `output`, optional `cachedInput`, `cacheWrite`, `cacheWrite1h`). Resolution at `model()` time: per-model `pricing` (`bedrock.model({ name, pricing })`) > SDK registry (exact id) > built-in profile price > `undefined` (no cost computed).

```ts
import { ai, totalCost } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import {
  BEDROCK_GLOBAL_PRICING,
  BedrockSDK,
  bedrockPricingFor,
  withClaudeCacheWriteRates,
} from "@warlock.js/ai-bedrock";

const bedrock = new BedrockSDK({
  region: "eu-west-1",
  pricing: {
    // In-Region and non-US geographic ids are not built in — price them yourself.
    "eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6": { input: 3.3, output: 16.5, cachedInput: 0.33 },
    "amazon.nova-pro-v1:0": { input: 0.8, output: 3.2 }, // your own rates for unlisted models
  },
});

bedrock.model({ name: "global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6" }).pricing; // built-in global rate
bedrock.model({ name: "eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6" }).pricing; // registry + Claude write rates filled (cacheWrite 4.125, cacheWrite1h 6.6)
bedrockPricingFor("us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"); // US geographic rate
withClaudeCacheWriteRates("anthropic.claude-opus-4-8", { input: 5, output: 25 }); // + cacheWrite 6.25, cacheWrite1h 10
Object.keys(BEDROCK_GLOBAL_PRICING); // the priced Claude model ids

const { usage } = await ai
  .agent({ model: bedrock.model({ name: "global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6" }) })
  .execute("hi");
console.log(usage.cost, totalCost(usage.cost)); // per-channel USD breakdown of THIS run, and its sum
```

- **Source.** https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/ — the page's own price feed for "US East (N. Virginia)", fetched 2026-10-17; model ids from the prompt-caching guide. `BEDROCK_GLOBAL_PRICING` holds the `global.` cross-Region profile rates, `BEDROCK_US_PRICING` the `us.` geographic rates (10% above global for these models). Both are keyed by the bare model id; `bedrockPricingFor(id)` strips the profile prefix.
- **Covered:** Claude Sonnet 5.5 / 5 / 4.6 / 4.5, Opus 5.5 / 5 / 4.8 / 4.7 / 4.6 / 4.5, Fable 5.1 / 5, Haiku 4.5 — with cache read, 5-minute write (1.25x input) and 1-hour write (2x input).
- **Deliberately unpriced:** in-Region ids with no profile prefix and other geographies (`eu.`, `apac.`, …) — their rates vary by Region; Claude Haiku 5.5 (not verified); and every non-Claude model (Nova, Llama, Titan, …). Pass `pricing` for them.
- **Claude write rates are filled.** Any Claude entry (your own included) without `cacheWrite` / `cacheWrite1h` gets 1.25x / 2x the input rate (`withClaudeCacheWriteRates`). Non-Claude entries are left as given; an unpriced cache write then bills at the input rate.

### Tokens & usage — cost truth

Both `complete()` and `stream()` normalize Converse's `TokenUsage` into the neutral `Usage` shape. With caching, `inputTokens` "represents only the non-cached input tokens" — total input is `inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheWriteInputTokens` (AWS prompt-caching guide) — so the adapter marks the usage `inputIncludesCache: false` and cost bills each channel once:

| Converse `TokenUsage` field | Neutral `Usage` field      | Notes                                                                |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `inputTokens`               | `usage.input`              | **Excludes** cache reads and writes. Bills at `pricing.input`.       |
| —                           | `usage.inputIncludesCache` | Always `false` on Bedrock.                                           |
| `outputTokens`              | `usage.output`             |                                                                      |
| `totalTokens`               | `usage.total`              | Falls back to `input + output` when absent.                          |
| `cacheReadInputTokens`      | `usage.cachedTokens`       | Only when `> 0`. Cache-hit reads — bills at `pricing.cachedInput`.   |
| `cacheWriteInputTokens`     | `usage.cacheWriteTokens`   | Only when `> 0`. Cache writes — bills at `pricing.cacheWrite`.       |
| `cacheDetails[ttl: "1h"]`   | `usage.cacheWrite1hTokens` | The 1-hour share of the writes — bills at `pricing.cacheWrite1h`.    |
| —                           | `usage.reasoningTokens`    | **Never set** — Converse exposes no reasoning-token count.           |
| —                           | `usage.cost`               | Attached on `complete()` and the streaming `done` chunk when priced. |

Read-side accounting is populated whenever Bedrock reports it, independent of whether you sent a `cacheControl` breakpoint.

## Provider body options and input-token counts

Native body fields merge after neutral options. When both values are plain
objects, their immediate keys merge and caller-provided keys win; untouched
neutral fields remain. Arrays, scalars and `null` replace the field. This merge
is one level deep: a nested object explicitly supplied by the caller replaces
that nested value.

`providerOptions.bedrock.body` adds native Converse request fields after the
neutral options, for completion and streaming:

```ts
const options = {
  reasoning: { effort: "high" as const }, // preserved alongside top_k
  providerOptions: { bedrock: { body: { additionalModelRequestFields: { top_k: 4 } } } },
};
await model.complete(messages, options);
```

The key stays `bedrock` for custom provider labels. Other provider keys are
ignored. `BedrockCallOptions` is exported. `modelId`, `messages`, `system` and
`toolConfig` are protected; attempting to replace them throws
`InvalidRequestError`. Provider fields are otherwise forwarded without validation.

`model.countTokens(messages, options?)` calls Bedrock `CountTokens` using the same
Converse messages, system blocks, tool configuration and
`additionalModelRequestFields` used for generation. Cancellation is forwarded.
Availability depends on the model and region; provider failures use the adapter's
normal typed errors. `sdk.count(text)` remains a separate offline estimate.

```ts
if (model.countTokens) {
  const inputTokens = await model.countTokens(messages, options);
}
```

## When NOT to use this skill

- Direct `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime` calls without going through `@warlock.js/ai` agents.
- OpenAI / Anthropic-direct / Gemini / Ollama models — those have their own adapter packages.
- Batch embeddings throughput — Titan is single-input upstream; use the OpenAI / Google / Ollama adapter (those batch natively).

## Adjacent conversation turns

Converse messages combine adjacent turns of the same role, retaining every
content block in order. This keeps parallel tool results in one user turn and
allows an automatic compaction summary beside an assistant tool-call turn
without creating consecutive assistant turns. Agent compaction frames a summary
as user context when it replaces the first non-system turn.

Adjacent-turn normalization preserves empty histories and separate system prompts
without inserting synthetic conversation turns.
